case_name: People's Union for Civil Liberties and another v State of Maharashtra and others
petitioner: People's Union for Civil Liberties and another
facts: On 03.09.2014, the arguments were heard on the question of the procedure to be followed in investigating police encounters.
The issue of genuineness or otherwise of nearly 99 encounters between the Mumbai police and the alleged criminals resulting in death of about 135 persons between 1995 and 1997 was raised.
PUCL filed three writ petitions before the Bombay High Court, which were later transferred to this Court.
People's Union for Civil Liberties (for short, 'PUCL') filed SLPs against the judgment and order dated 22-25.02.1999.
issues: The procedure to be followed in investigating police encounters.
Genuineness or otherwise of nearly 99 encounters between the Mumbai police and the alleged criminals resulting in death of about 135 persons between 1995 and 1997.
petitioner_arguments: There is no need to notice the facts of the three writ petitions in detail.
The guidelines issued by the National Human Rights Commission (for short, 'NHRC') should be followed.
The police should avoid any iota of delay under any circumstances whatsoever.
respondent_arguments: No arguments were presented by the respondents.
It is not necessary to notice the facts of the three writ petitions in detail.
court_reasoning: The guarantee by Art. 21 is available to every person and even the State has no authority to violate that right.
The Court issued certain directives as preventive measures in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal.
The police needs to be infused with basic human values and made sensitive to the Constitutional ethos.
holding: The guidelines issued by the National Human Rights Commission (for short, 'NHRC') should be followed.
The police should avoid any iota of delay under any circumstances whatsoever.
The Court directed issuance of notice to the Union of India, States and Union Territories for consideration of issuance of final directions / guidelines in the matter.
